MCI.verdict: The most dangerous attack in the league and it never takes its foot off: 2.44 xG per 90 when ahead, more than when level. Best chance quality going (0.14 a shot, 38 box touches).
MCI.fpl: Haaland is the armband every week they play a side that tries to play. The catch is Maresca: he rotates (2.2 changes a match) and hooks early (first change 56'), so anyone not called Haaland is a minutes gamble.
MCI.gw: Away at Arsenal: Haaland's worst fixture of the run. City still create (2.04 xG a match) but Arsenal give away the fewest chances in the league.

FUL.verdict: A good-looking ball side that gets into the box (32 touches a match) and never panics: settled eleven, latest changes in the league (68').
FUL.fpl: Minutes are bankable, but they give chances away when level (1.43 per 90), so their defenders are not.
FUL.gw: Home to Bournemouth: Fulham keep the ball but give chances away.

ARS.verdict: Still the best team: 0.83 xG conceded a match even after 2-2 at Newcastle. Ødegaard has taken over corners.
ARS.fpl: The defence is the asset. Gabriel has started all 10 and played 90 every time. The goals spread across the attack, so no single forward is a lock.
ARS.gw: Home to City: the hardest match of their run, then BRE, TOT, BOU, MUN. Gabriel's value is the five weeks, not this one.

NEW.verdict: Chaos. They run hard, rotate, attack whatever the score and leave the door open (1.67 xG conceded). When the game is level they barely create (0.76 per 90).
NEW.fpl: Target attackers against them. Avoid their defenders.
NEW.gw: Away at Brighton: Newcastle concede plenty; their attackers chase games.

AVL.verdict: Good when level, loose once ahead (they conceded 3.11 per 90 when leading earlier), but their attack is creating again.
AVL.fpl: Villa defenders are a trap. Their games stay open, which suits N.Jackson and whoever faces them.
AVL.gw: Away at the league's most open defence. N.Jackson (penalties, 6 goals) is the armband shout; Villa clean sheet unlikely.

SUN.verdict: They shoot from good positions (0.13 a shot) but can't keep games tight (1.64 conceded) and have hardly led all season.
SUN.fpl: Nothing at the back. Attackers only in open games.
SUN.gw: Home to Spurs: Sunderland chase hard when behind and shoot from good spots.

BOU.verdict: The most complete side outside the top two. They win the ball back (27.7 a match), concede only 10.3 shots, create quality chances (0.13 a shot), and play the same whether ahead or level. Rose trusts his eleven and changes late.
BOU.fpl: Their defenders are real, which is why keeping Silva was right. Tavernier starts every week and gets good chances (4.2 xG).
BOU.gw: Away at Fulham: Bournemouth create quality chances (0.13 a shot); Silva benched this week only because Fulham have the ball at home.

NFO.verdict: Deep block, win it back, break. Hard to break down (10 shots conceded a match), but they take long shots and only come alive once ahead.
NFO.fpl: Sneaky defenders, low-quality attack. Gibbs-White creates (2.6 xA) but has one goal.
NFO.gw: Home to Chelsea, who just lost 1-4 at home to Leeds and go flat when behind. Forest keep teams to 10 shots a match: a tight one, a decent Forest clean-sheet shout.

CHE.verdict: Alonso's side is coming apart: 1-4 at home to Leeds, 20 goals conceded in 11 (1.60 xG a match), shoot from distance (low quality chances), rotate 2.7 changes a match and go flat behind (0.76 per 90).
CHE.fpl: Only the nailed core: Palmer and Rogers have started 10 of 10. Everyone else is a coin flip on minutes. The defence is not a buy.
CHE.gw: Away at Forest's block: low chance quality. Palmer and Rogers are nailed but this is not a week to want Chelsea attackers.

LEE.verdict: Farke's Leeds are the form side outside the top four: 4-1 at Chelsea, hard to create against now (1.19 xG conceded a match), a settled eleven and late changes.
LEE.fpl: Calvert-Lewin is the whole attack (4.4 xG). Bogle is nailed.
LEE.gw: Home to Coventry, who sit deep and score 1.04 a match. Leeds clean sheet is a good shout; Calvert-Lewin (penalties, 3 headers at Chelsea) gets the box chances against a team that defends the box.

COV.verdict: Lampard sits deep (39% possession), defends the box, protects a lead and goes flat behind. A low-event team.
COV.fpl: Rudoni is their threat (2.2 xG, 1.7 xA). Clean sheets are shaky (1.5 xG conceded).
COV.gw: Away at Leeds: a low-event match. Coventry attackers have little.

CRY.verdict: Frank lost his first game 3-2 at Coventry. The defence is still the league's worst (2.15 xG conceded a match).
CRY.fpl: Attack them until Frank shows otherwise.
CRY.gw: Home to Hull: attack them until Frank fixes it.

TOT.verdict: De Zerbi's side has the ball (63%) but shoots from distance (0.08 a shot): sterile up front, solid at the back (1.2 conceded). Rotates and hooks early (56').
TOT.fpl: The value is at the back: Kinsky and Van Hecke. The attackers frustrate.
TOT.gw: Away at Sunderland: Spurs are solid (1.13 conceded) but shoot from distance.

IPS.verdict: Open at both ends. They shoot well but concede 1.95 a match.
IPS.fpl: Davis is nailed, but the defence behind him is not a clean-sheet side, so selling him is right.
IPS.gw: Home to Villa: Ipswich concede 2.02 xG a match, the most in the league, and open further when chasing.

HUL.verdict: 5-4-1 low block with 33% of the ball, and they fold once ahead (2.29 conceded per 90 when leading).
HUL.gw: Away at Palace's open defence after beating Brighton 2-0: Hull attackers have a shot.

BHA.verdict: Second-best attack (1.97 xG a match) but they lost 2-0 at Hull with 2.24 xG; flat when behind now. A settled eleven.
BHA.fpl: Groß is the attacking pick (4 goals, 6 assists, set pieces). De Cuyper has played left wing only while Mitoma is out (hamstring, back 2 Dec); once Mitoma returns he is a left-back again. Vuskovic and Verbruggen are the defence.
BHA.gw: Home to Newcastle, who open up (1.65 conceded) and chase when behind. Good for De Cuyper and Groß; a clean sheet is a 50-50.

LIV.verdict: Iraola's Liverpool are scoring freely again (4-0 against United, 1.78 xG a match) and chase hard when behind.
LIV.fpl: Their attackers return in chase games. Their defenders do fine when protecting a lead (0.83 conceded per 90 when ahead).
LIV.gw: Away at Everton's deep block: harder than the 4-0 suggests, but Wirtz (2 goals, 6 assists, penalties) is the creator.

MUN.verdict: Pochettino has one match in charge (0-4 at Liverpool). Under Carrick they opened up (1.99 conceded a match).
MUN.gw: Home to Brentford: new-manager week, so read it carefully; the defence they inherit is among the worst.

EVE.verdict: Moyes's Everton are organised and settled, but they sit on leads and go flat behind. A low ceiling.
EVE.fpl: Barry carries the attack. Little else.
EVE.gw: Home to Liverpool after a 0-4 at Brentford. Everton sit deep and defend the box, but go flat behind.

BRE.verdict: Andrews' Brentford win it back, keep attacking when ahead (4-0 against Everton) and rotate a little.
BRE.fpl: Attackers in home games. The defence leaks shots.
BRE.gw: Away at a United side conceding 1.99 a match under a manager in his second game. Good for Brentford attackers.

players.4: In for Davis. Best defender in the best defence; five-week value (MCI, BRE, TOT, BOU, MUN), not one week.
players.166: Captain. Away at Ipswich, the most open defence in the league; he takes Villa's penalties.
players.346: Vice. Home to Coventry's deep block; on penalties and headers, 6 shots and 1.34 xG at Chelsea.
players.411: Not the armband this week: away at Arsenal. Keep him; LEE, BRE, CHE, HUL follow.
players.366: 14 points last week. Away at Everton's block, but he creates everything for Liverpool.
players.124: Home to Newcastle; Brighton's set pieces and 4 goals, 6 assists.
players.68: Away at Fulham; nailed, 5 goals, on Bournemouth's penalties.
players.330: Home to Coventry, a strong Leeds clean-sheet shout.
players.109: Home to Newcastle; a 50-50 clean sheet.
players.40: Bench: Chelsea away at Forest's block.
players.566: Bench this week only (Fulham away); back in from GW14.
players.8: Bench: City at home is the hardest Arsenal match; Saliba's return could rotate the back line.
players.45: In for Palmer: Villa's right winger, started his last five with 2 goals and 2 assists; IPS away, EVE and CRY at home next.
players.504: Kept. Same Brighton defence as De Cuyper, and De Cuyper's winger role ends when Mitoma returns (2 Dec).
